[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-005-design-system-migration-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Many ASP.NET applications use Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX and DevExpress server controls that cannot be reused in React applications. These server-side components render only in ASP.NET runtime and cannot export to npm packages. Teams migrating from ASP.NET to React must rebuild all healthcare-specific UI components (member cards, claim grids, provider listings, authorization workflows) creating duplication of effort across multiple migration projects.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-005-design-system-migration-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

The Design System Migration pattern defines development of an enterprise React component library replacing Telerik/DevExpress with accessible, reusable React components distributed via npm. The pattern includes component architecture, Storybook documentation, accessibility testing framework, npm publishing pipeline, and migration mapping from Telerik/DevExpress to React equivalents.

### When to Use

- **ASP.NET → React Migrations**: Teams completing PTN-APP-MFE-013 need React component equivalents
- **Cross-Product Consistency**: Multiple applications require shared UI components
- **Telerik/DevExpress License Reduction**: Eliminate per-developer licensing costs for server-control libraries that cannot be reused in React
- **Accessibility Compliance**: Section 508/WCAG 2.2 AA requirements for all applications
- **Component Sharing**: Micro-frontends need shared design system for visual consistency

- **Eliminate Duplication**: Build components once, reuse across all applications
- **Cost Savings**: Reduce per-developer licensing costs for Telerik/DevExpress libraries not usable in React

### Business Context

**Migration Reality:**
- ASP.NET applications require React component equivalents for all Telerik/DevExpress server controls
- Components must support healthcare workflows (claims, eligibility, care coordination)

**Current State:**
- Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX (2025.x versions) - server controls only
- DevExpress ASP.NET (22.x-24.x versions) - server controls only
- Custom ASP.NET User Controls - cannot export to React/npm
- Licensing costs: Per-developer annual licensing for libraries not portable to React
- Components not reusable across products (licensing boundaries)

**Target State:**
- React component library with 50-100 components
- Published to private npm registry (@gainwell/design-system)
- Storybook documentation with healthcare examples
- Accessibility testing pipeline (axe-core, pa11y)
- Versioned releases following semantic versioning

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-005-design-system-migration-pattern.md#problem-details]

### Problem Details

**Problem 1: Server Control Architecture**

Telerik/DevExpress components are ASP.NET server controls:

```aspx
<%-- Telerik Server Control - Cannot reuse in React --%>
<telerik:RadGrid ID="ClaimsGrid" runat="server"
    AutoGenerateColumns="False"
    AllowPaging="True" PageSize="25"
    AllowSorting="True" AllowFilteringByColumn="True"
    OnNeedDataSource="ClaimsGrid_NeedDataSource">
    <MasterTableView>
        <Columns>
            <telerik:GridBoundColumn DataField="ClaimId" HeaderText="Claim ID" />
            <telerik:GridBoundColumn DataField="Amount" HeaderText="Amount" DataFormatString="{0:C}" />
        </Columns>
    </MasterTableView>
</telerik:RadGrid>
```

**Impact:**
- Cannot export server controls to npm packages
- Must completely rebuild in React
- 100+ component variations to recreate

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-005-design-system-migration-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

**Competing Forces:**

- **Build vs. Buy**: Building custom design system vs. adopting third-party library (Material-UI, Ant Design) with licensing/customization costs
- **Comprehensive vs. Phased**: Build all 60-85 components upfront (24 weeks) vs. build incrementally as teams need them (risk of inconsistency)
- **Healthcare-Specific vs. Generic**: Custom healthcare components (MemberCard, ClaimGrid) vs. generic components with configuration overhead
- **Accessibility vs. Speed**: WCAG 2.2 AA compliance adds 30-40% development time but is legally required
- **Innovation vs. Standardization**: Allow teams flexibility in component variations vs. strict design system compliance

**Technical Constraints:**

- **React Version Compatibility**: Must support React 18+ and be compatible with Module Federation remote entry loading
- **Bundle Size**: Each component must be <25KB gzipped to avoid performance degradation in micro-frontends
- **Browser Support**: IE11 no longer required (end of life), focus on modern browsers (Chrome 90+, Firefox 88+, Edge 90+, Safari 14+)
- **TypeScript**: All components must be TypeScript-first with proper type definitions exported
- **Build Tool**: Must work with both Webpack 5 (current) and Vite (future) build systems

**Organizational Constraints:**

- **Team Capacity**: 2-3 senior developers available for design system development (not full-time, 50-60% allocation)
- **Design Resources**: UX designers available part-time (20-30% allocation), healthcare domain expertise required
- **Migration Timeline**: Multiple applications migrating over 3-5 years, design system must be production-ready within 6 months
- **Maintenance Burden**: Who maintains design system long-term? Dedicated team vs. shared ownership model
- **Versioning Strategy**: How to handle breaking changes when 20+ teams depend on components

**Business Constraints:**

- **License Costs**: Telerik/DevExpress per-developer licensing savings must justify design system investment
- **Training Requirements**: All React developers need training on design system usage and contribution guidelines
- **Documentation Burden**: Storybook documentation must be maintained, healthcare-specific examples required
- **Adoption Resistance**: Teams may prefer third-party libraries (Material-UI familiarity) over custom design system

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-005-design-system-migration-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

Develop enterprise React component library with:

1. **Component Architecture**: Atomic design (atoms, molecules, organisms)
2. **Accessibility First**: WCAG 2.2 AA compliance built-in
3. **Healthcare-Specific**: Components for Medicaid/Medicare workflows
4. **Storybook Documentation**: Interactive examples and usage guidelines
5. **npm Publishing**: Private Artifactory registry (@gainwell/design-system)
6. **Versioning Strategy**: Semantic versioning with migration guides
7. **Testing Pipeline**: Unit tests (Vitest), accessibility tests (axe-core)

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-005-design-system-migration-pattern.md#components]

### Components

| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
|-----------|----------------|--------------|
| **Component Library (@gainwell/design-system)** | Provide reusable React components (60-85 components); manage component state, props, and variants; export TypeScript type definitions; ensure WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility | React 18+, TypeScript 5+, styled-components or CSS modules, accessibility testing libraries (axe-core) |
| **Storybook Documentation** | Document all components with interactive examples; provide healthcare-specific use cases; demonstrate accessibility features; enable component playground for developers | Storybook 7+, MDX for documentation, Storybook addons (a11y, controls, docs) |
| **Accessibility Testing Framework** | Automate WCAG 2.2 AA compliance testing; run axe-core and pa11y on all components; generate accessibility reports; integrate with CI/CD pipeline | axe-core, pa11y, jest-axe, Cypress with axe plugin |
| **npm Publishing Pipeline** | Build and bundle components; generate TypeScript definitions; publish versioned releases to Artifactory; automate semantic versioning; create changelogs | Rollup or Webpack, TypeScript compiler, npm scripts, GitHub Actions or Azure DevOps |
| **Design Tokens** | Define color palette, typography, spacing, breakpoints; export tokens as CSS variables and JavaScript/TypeScript; ensure consistency across components; support theming (light/dark mode) | Style Dictionary or custom token generator, CSS custom properties |
| **Migration Mapping Guide** | Map Telerik/DevExpress components to React equivalents; provide code examples for common patterns; document API differences; offer codemods for automated migration where possible | Documentation site (Docusaurus or MkDocs), component mapping matrix |
| **Healthcare-Specific Components** | Provide domain-specific components (MemberCard, ClaimGrid, ProviderListing, AuthorizationWorkflow); implement Medicaid/Medicare business logic; ensure HIPAA-compliant display of PHI | Base design system components, healthcare data models, PHI masking utilities |
| **Version Management** | Track component versions using semantic versioning; maintain compatibility matrix (React versions, browser support); communicate breaking changes; provide migration guides for major versions | package.json versioning, CHANGELOG.md, migration documentation |

### Interactions

**Component Development Workflow:**

```text
1. UX Designer → Designs component in Figma
2. Designer → Exports design tokens (colors, spacing, typography)
3. Developer → Creates React component in design-system repo
4. Developer → Writes unit tests (Jest) + accessibility tests (jest-axe)
5. Developer → Documents component in Storybook with healthcare examples
6. CI/CD Pipeline → Runs tests, builds component, publishes to Artifactory
7. Consuming Team → Installs latest version: npm install @gainwell/design-system@latest
8. Consuming Team → Imports component: import { MemberCard } from '@gainwell/design-system'
```

**Component Usage Flow:**

```text
Application Team → Discovers component in Storybook documentation
                → Reviews healthcare examples (member card with PHI masking)
                → Installs design system: npm install @gainwell/design-system
                → Imports component: import { MemberCard } from '@gainwell/design-system'
                → Uses component with props: <MemberCard member={memberData} onSelect={handleSelect} />
                → Component handles accessibility (ARIA labels, keyboard navigation)
                → Component applies design tokens (colors, spacing, typography)
```

**Migration Workflow (Telerik → React):**

```text
1. Team identifies Telerik component: RadGrid with 10 columns, sorting, pagination
2. Team consults Migration Mapping Guide: RadGrid → Table component
3. Team reviews Table component in Storybook: sorting, filtering, pagination examples
4. Team migrates code:
   - Before: <telerik:RadGrid ID="ClaimsGrid" runat="server" ...>
   - After: <Table columns={claimsColumns} data={claimsData} sortable paginated />
5. Team tests accessibility: keyboard navigation, screen reader compatibility
6. Team verifies healthcare requirements: PHI masking, HIPAA compliance
```

**Version Update Flow:**

```text
Design System Team → Releases v2.1.0 with new Table filter feature
                   → Publishes to Artifactory (npm publish)
                   → Updates CHANGELOG.md with breaking changes
                   → Notifies teams via Slack/Teams announcement

Application Team → Reviews changelog for breaking changes
                → Updates package.json: "@gainwell/design-system": "^2.1.0"
                → Runs npm install
                → Tests application with new version
                → Deploys with updated components
```

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-005-design-system-migration-pattern.md#variations]

### Variations

**Variation 1: Monorepo Design System (Recommended)**

- **Structure**: Single repo with packages/ directory containing multiple packages (@gainwell/components, @gainwell/tokens, @gainwell/icons)
- **Use Case**: Large design system with 60-85 components, shared tokens across packages
- **Advantages**: Centralized versioning, easier cross-package refactoring, shared build pipeline
- **Disadvantages**: Longer CI/CD pipeline (must build all packages), larger repo size
- **Tools**: Turborepo, Lerna, or Nx for monorepo management

**Variation 2: Multi-Repo Design System**

- **Structure**: Separate repos for @gainwell/components, @gainwell/tokens, @gainwell/icons
- **Use Case**: Small teams, independent package versioning, decentralized ownership
- **Advantages**: Faster CI/CD per package, independent release cycles, smaller repos
- **Disadvantages**: Versioning complexity (token updates require component updates), duplicate build configuration
- **Tools**: Standard npm packages, GitHub/GitLab repos

**Variation 3: Third-Party Base + Custom Healthcare Components**

- **Structure**: Adopt Material-UI or Ant Design for base components (Button, Input), build only healthcare-specific components (MemberCard, ClaimGrid) as @gainwell/healthcare-components
- **Use Case**: Faster time-to-market, leverage existing design system, focus on healthcare domain
- **Advantages**: Reduced development cost vs. custom build, proven accessibility, large community
- **Disadvantages**: License costs (Material-UI Pro $588/developer annually), less brand control, potential conflicts with Gainwell branding
- **Recommendation**: Consider for pilot projects, evaluate long-term licensing costs

**Variation 4: Design System as Micro-Frontend**

- **Structure**: Design system components loaded as Module Federation remote entry, consumed by shell at runtime
- **Use Case**: Centralized component updates without application redeployment, A/B testing of component variants
- **Advantages**: Hot-swappable components, instant updates across all applications, centralized component version management
- **Disadvantages**: Runtime dependency on design system remote, increased complexity, potential network latency
- **Recommendation**: Experimental, not recommended for production (stability concerns)

   ```bash

   npx storybook@latest init

   # Testing
   npm install --save-dev vitest @testing-library/react @testing-library/jest-dom
   npm install --save-dev @axe-core/react jest-axe

   # Build
   npm install --save-dev @rollup/plugin-typescript rollup-plugin-peer-deps-external
   ```

3. **Implement 10 Core Atoms**
   - Button (primary, secondary, tertiary, danger, sizes)
   - Input (text, password, email, number, disabled states)

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-005-design-system-migration-pattern.md#best-practices]

### Best Practices

- **Accessibility First**: Every component must pass axe-core automated tests
- **Keyboard Navigation**: All interactive components support keyboard-only operation
- **TypeScript Strict**: Enable strict mode for type safety
- **Prop Consistency**: Use consistent naming (disabled, loading, fullWidth, etc.)
- **Compound Components**: Use composition patterns for flexibility
- **Healthcare Terminology**: Use payer-centric terms (member, claim, provider)
- **Version Deprecation**: Provide 2-version migration window for breaking changes

### Common Pitfalls

- **Pitfall 1: Over-Engineering Components**
  - Start simple, add features as needed by consuming applications
  - Don't build features speculatively

- **Pitfall 2: Skipping Accessibility Testing**
  - Accessibility bugs discovered late are expensive to fix
  - Run axe-core on every component in CI/CD

- **Pitfall 3: No Migration Documentation**
  - Teams need Telerik → React mapping guides
  - Document component API differences clearly

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-005-design-system-migration-pattern.md#real-world-example-1-member-card-component-development]

### Real-World Example 1: Member Card Component Development

**Context:**
- 15 Gainwell applications (Member Eligibility, Care Management, Provider Portal) display member information inconsistently
- Each application built custom member card UI component with varying PHI masking approaches
- Accessibility compliance varies (60-80% WCAG 2.2 AA across applications)
- Telerik RadDataForm used in 8 ASP.NET applications but cannot be reused in React
- Estimated 3-5 days per application to rebuild member card component

**Implementation:**
1. **Requirements Gathering** (Week 1):
   - Surveyed multiple applications: identified common member fields (ID, name, DOB, eligibility status, coverage, care manager)
   - Defined PHI masking requirements: SSN last 4 digits, DOB optional based on user role
   - UX designer created Figma mockups: compact vs. full variants, color-coded eligibility status badges

2. **Component Development** (Week 2):
   - Built React component with TypeScript: `<MemberCard member={memberData} variant="compact" | "full" onAction={handler} />`
   - Implemented accessibility: ARIA landmarks (region), labels, keyboard-accessible actions
   - Added PHI masking utilities: `maskSSN('123-45-6789')` returns `'XXX-XX-6789'`
   - Created 3 variants: compact (name, ID, status), full (+ coverage, care manager), grid (minimal for tables)

3. **Documentation & Testing** (Week 3):
   - Documented in Storybook: 5 healthcare examples (Medicaid, Medicare, dual-eligible, managed care, uninsured)
   - Wrote unit tests: Jest + React Testing Library (95% coverage)
   - Accessibility testing: axe-core (0 violations), manual JAWS/NVDA testing

4. **Release & Adoption** (Week 4):
   - Published v1.0.0 to Artifactory: `@gainwell/design-system@1.0.0`
   - Migration guide: Telerik RadDataForm → MemberCard mapping
   - Teams adopted over 6 months: multiple applications migrated

**Before (Telerik ASP.NET):**
```aspx
<telerik:RadDataForm ID="MemberCard" runat="server"
    DataSourceID="MemberDataSource"
    CssClass="member-card">
    <ItemTemplate>
        <asp:Label ID="MemberName" runat="server" Text='<%# Eval("Name") %>' />
        <asp:Label ID="MemberID" runat="server" Text='<%# Eval("MemberId") %>' />
    </ItemTemplate>
</telerik:RadDataForm>
```

**After (React Design System):**
```typescript
import { MemberCard } from '@gainwell/design-system';

<MemberCard
  member={{
    id: 'M123456',
    name: 'John Doe',
    dateOfBirth: '1985-03-15',
    eligibilityStatus: 'Active',
    coverage: 'Full Medicaid'
  }}
  variant="full"
  onViewDetails={(memberId) => navigate(`/members/${memberId}`)}
  onEditMember={(memberId) => openEditModal(memberId)}
/>
```

**Outcome:**
- **Reuse Across Applications**: Multiple applications using MemberCard (4-5 days saved per application)
- **Consistent PHI Masking**: Reduced HIPAA compliance risk with centralized masking logic
- **Accessibility**: 100% WCAG 2.2 AA compliance (vs. 60-80% with custom implementations)
- **Developer Experience**: 15-minute integration (vs. 3-5 days building from scratch)
- **Maintenance**: Bug fix in MemberCard benefits all applications using it (update once, deploy independently)

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-005-design-system-migration-pattern.md#real-world-example-2-telerik-radgrid-migration-to-react-table]

### Real-World Example 2: Telerik RadGrid Migration to React Table

**Context:**
- Ohio MMIS Claims application with Telerik RadGrid displaying 50,000+ claims
- Grid features: 10 columns, sorting, filtering, pagination (25 rows/page), Excel export
- ASP.NET server-side data binding with ViewState (slow performance, 2-3 second page loads)
- Team migrating to React micro-frontend, need equivalent table component
- Telerik RadGrid license: per-developer annual fee for team

**Implementation:**
1. **Component Selection** (Day 1):
   - Evaluated design system Table component in Storybook: sorting, filtering, pagination, virtual scrolling
   - Confirmed feature parity: all RadGrid features available in React Table
   - Reviewed migration mapping guide: RadGrid props → Table props

2. **Data Migration** (Days 2-3):
   - Replaced ASP.NET server-side data binding with React Query for client-side fetching
   - Backend API remained unchanged: `/api/claims?page=1&pageSize=25&sortBy=claimId`
   - Implemented optimistic UI updates: instant sorting/filtering without server round-trip

3. **Component Migration** (Days 4-5):
   ```typescript
   // Before: Telerik RadGrid (ASP.NET)
   // <telerik:RadGrid ID="ClaimsGrid" runat="server" AllowPaging="True" PageSize="25" ...>

   // After: React Table
   import { Table } from '@gainwell/design-system';

   const columns = [
     { field: 'claimId', header: 'Claim ID', sortable: true, filterable: true },
     { field: 'memberId', header: 'Member ID', sortable: true },
     { field: 'amount', header: 'Amount', formatter: (val) => `$${val.toFixed(2)}`, sortable: true },
     { field: 'status', header: 'Status', sortable: true, filterable: true },
     { field: 'submittedDate', header: 'Submitted', formatter: formatDate, sortable: true }
   ];

   <Table
     columns={columns}
     data={claims}
     loading={isLoading}
     paginated
     pageSize={25}
     sortable
     filterable
     virtualScroll
     onRowClick={(claim) => navigate(`/claims/${claim.claimId}`)}
   />
   ```

4. **Testing & Deployment** (Days 6-7):
   - Performance testing: 50,000 claims with virtual scrolling (60fps scrolling)
   - Accessibility testing: keyboard navigation (arrow keys, Enter, Tab), screen reader compatible
   - Deployed via blue-green deployment: zero downtime

**Outcome:**
- **Performance**: Page load time reduced from 2-3 seconds to 0.5 seconds (6x faster)
- **License Savings**: Per-developer Telerik license eliminated for team members now using React design system
- **Bundle Size**: RadGrid 450KB → Table 25KB (18x smaller)
- **Accessibility**: WCAG 2.2 AA compliant (keyboard navigation, ARIA labels built-in)
- **Migration Time**: 7 days (vs. 14-21 days building table component from scratch)
- **User Experience**: Instant sorting/filtering (client-side), no page reloads

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-005-design-system-migration-pattern.md#scenario-1-migrating-telerik-radgrid-to-react-table]

#### Scenario 1: Migrating Telerik RadGrid to React Table

**When to Use:**
- ASP.NET application with Telerik RadGrid displaying claims data
- Team migrating to React micro-frontend architecture
- Need sorting, filtering, pagination, and Excel export

**Approach:**
1. Review Table component in Storybook: claims example with 10 columns, sorting, filtering
2. Map Telerik RadGrid properties to React Table props:
   - `AutoGenerateColumns="False"` → Define columns array with field, header, formatter
   - `AllowPaging="True" PageSize="25"` → `paginated pageSize={25}`
   - `AllowSorting="True"` → `sortable defaultSort={{ field: 'claimId', direction: 'asc' }}`
   - `AllowFilteringByColumn="True"` → `filterable filters={columnFilters}`
3. Implement data fetching with React Query or Redux for backend API calls
4. Add accessibility: keyboard navigation (arrow keys), ARIA labels, screen reader announcements
5. Test with healthcare data: 50,000+ claims, PHI masking (member SSN, DOB)

**Outcome:**
- Migration time: 2-3 days per RadGrid instance
- Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA compliant by default (Telerik required manual ARIA fixes)
- Performance: Virtual scrolling handles 50,000+ rows (Telerik limited to 10,000 rows)
- License savings: $2,000-$5,000 per developer annually

#### Scenario 2: Building Healthcare-Specific MemberCard Component

**When to Use:**
- Multiple applications need consistent member information display
- Member data includes PHI (SSN, DOB, address) requiring proper masking
- Eligibility status, coverage type, and care manager assignment displayed
- Medicaid/Medicare programs have specific display requirements

**Approach:**
1. Design component API: `<MemberCard member={memberData} variant="compact" | "full" onAction={handler} />`
2. Implement PHI masking: SSN shows last 4 digits (XXX-XX-1234), DOB optional display based on user role
3. Add eligibility status indicator: color-coded badge (Active=green, Pending=yellow, Terminated=red)
4. Support variants: compact (name, ID, status), full (+ coverage, care manager, last visit)
5. Accessibility: ARIA landmarks (region), labels, keyboard-accessible action buttons
6. Document in Storybook: 5+ healthcare examples (Medicaid, Medicare, dual-eligible, managed care)

**Outcome:**
- Reused across 15+ applications (Member Eligibility, Care Management, Provider Portal)
- Consistent PHI masking reduces HIPAA compliance risk
- Development time: 1 week to build, saves 4-5 days per application (no rebuild)
- Accessibility: Screen reader tested with JAWS/NVDA

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-005-design-system-migration-pattern.md#scenario-3-replacing-devexpress-datepicker-with-accessible-react-datepicker]

#### Scenario 3: Replacing DevExpress DatePicker with Accessible React DatePicker

**When to Use:**
- Date input required for claim submission dates, member DOB, authorization dates
- DevExpress DateEdit control replaced during ASP.NET → React migration
- Accessibility requirements: keyboard navigation, screen reader support

**Approach:**
1. Evaluate date picker options: @gainwell/design-system DatePicker vs. third-party (react-datepicker, react-day-picker)
2. Build design system DatePicker with features:
   - Date range selection (claim date range queries)
   - Locale support (Spanish for Puerto Rico MMIS)
   - Min/max date constraints (no future dates for claim submission)
   - Keyboard navigation: arrow keys navigate calendar, Enter selects, Escape closes
   - ARIA: role="dialog", aria-label="Select date", aria-selected
3. Document healthcare examples: claim submission date (past only), appointment scheduling (future only), eligibility effective dates (range)
4. Test with screen readers: JAWS announces "Select date dialog, January 2026, press arrow keys to navigate"

**Outcome:**
- Replaces DevExpress DateEdit across 80+ forms
- Accessibility: 100% keyboard accessible, screen reader compatible
- Locale support: English + Spanish for PR MMIS
- Bundle size: 12KB gzipped (DevExpress was 150KB)

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-005-design-system-migration-pattern.md#before-telerikdevexpress-aspnet-controls]

#### Before (Telerik/DevExpress ASP.NET Controls)

**Developer Experience:**
- **Component Discovery**: Search Telerik documentation (1,000+ controls), no healthcare-specific examples
- **Installation**: Download Telerik installer, install per developer machine, license key per project
- **Usage**: Drag-and-drop from Visual Studio toolbox or write ASP.NET markup
- **Customization**: Override CSS classes, limited control over HTML output
- **Accessibility**: Manual ARIA attributes, no accessibility testing in CI/CD
- **Versioning**: Telerik version locked per project (2025.1, 2025.2), upgrade all controls simultaneously

**Technical Implementation:**
```aspx
<%-- ASP.NET Page with Telerik RadGrid --%>
<telerik:RadGrid ID="ClaimsGrid" runat="server"
    AutoGenerateColumns="False"
    AllowPaging="True" PageSize="25"
    AllowSorting="True" AllowFilteringByColumn="True"
    OnNeedDataSource="ClaimsGrid_NeedDataSource">
    <MasterTableView>
        <Columns>
            <telerik:GridBoundColumn DataField="ClaimId" HeaderText="Claim ID" />
            <telerik:GridBoundColumn DataField="Amount" HeaderText="Amount" DataFormatString="{0:C}" />
        </Columns>
    </MasterTableView>
</telerik:RadGrid>

<script runat="server">
protected void ClaimsGrid_NeedDataSource(object sender, GridNeedDataSourceEventArgs e)
{
    ClaimsGrid.DataSource = GetClaims(); // Server-side C# data binding
}
</script>
```

**Challenges:**
- Server-side data binding prevents client-side interactivity
- 30-second deployment downtime (IIS app pool recycle)
- License costs: $2,000-$5,000 per developer annually
- 150KB+ bundle size per control (RadGrid = 450KB)
- Limited TypeScript support, no type safety

### Dependencies

**Required Patterns:**

- **PTN-APP-MFE-007 (Build Infrastructure)**: npm registry (Artifactory or CodeArtifact) required for publishing design system packages
- **PTN-APP-MFE-013 (ASP.NET Migration)**: Design system enables React migrations by providing Telerik/DevExpress replacements

**Required Standards:**

- **STD-APP-ACCESS-001 (Accessibility Standard)**: WCAG 2.2 AA compliance required for all components
- **STD-APP-ARCH-001 (Application Architecture)**: Component architecture patterns (composition, props, state management)

**Required Technologies:**

- **React 18+**: Component library built with React hooks, Context API, and modern patterns
- **TypeScript 5+**: All components require TypeScript definitions for type safety
- **npm Registry**: Private registry (Artifactory or AWS CodeArtifact) for package distribution
- **Storybook 7+**: Component documentation and interactive playground
- **Accessibility Tools**: axe-core, pa11y, jest-axe for automated testing

**Optional Dependencies:**

- **Design Tool**: Figma or Sketch for design collaboration and token export
- **Monorepo Tool**: Turborepo, Lerna, or Nx if adopting monorepo structure
- **Testing Library**: React Testing Library for component unit tests

## TL;DR

**Problem:** ASP.NET applications use Telerik/DevExpress server controls that cannot be reused in React. Must rebuild all healthcare UI components across multiple migration projects.

**Solution:** Enterprise React component library (@gainwell/design-system) with 60-85 components replacing Telerik/DevExpress, published to npm, documented in Storybook.

**Key Benefits:**
- **Eliminate Duplication**: Build once, reuse across all applications
- **Cost Savings**: Reduce Telerik/DevExpress per-developer licensing costs for migrated applications
- **Accessibility Built-In**: WCAG 2.2 AA compliance

**Implementation Complexity:** **High** (16-24 weeks, requires design system expertise and cross-team partnership)

**Related Patterns:** [ASP.NET Migration](./PTN-APP-MFE-013-pattern.md) | [Module Composition](./PTN-APP-MFE-003-pattern.md)
